summary.headline: Shree Refrigerations H1 FY27 revenue rose about 84-85% YoY to roughly INR 100 crore, with EBITDA margin up to 13.5% from 11%; FY27 margin guided at about 22%.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue was roughly INR 100 crore, up about 84-85% YoY, and EBITDA margin improved to 13.5% from 11% despite commodity inflation. Management reiterated 40% revenue CAGR and about 22% annual EBITDA margin guidance, while H1 margins remain skewed low versus H2. Order book stood at about INR 198.6-200 crore at September, down from INR 270 crore at the start of the year, and operating cash flow was negative about INR 42 crore in H1. Management said the data centre opportunity is excluded from guidance and is expected to take 6-12 months to gain traction.

financial_highlights.change: Up about 84-85% YoY vs H1 FY26
Down from INR 270 crore at start of year
Up from INR 105 crore; about 250 days
Up from about 370 days after IPO-era improvement

segments.name: Refrigeration vertical (HVAC, AC plant, Ref plant)
segments.commentary: Management reports a single refrigeration vertical with no separate product segments; HVAC is a larger share than AC plant, and Ref plant is a very small share. Retrofit is the major business line, with defence spares a large component, alongside installation, commissioning and service.

segments.name: Non-defence / industrial
segments.commentary: Industrial chillers and test equipment are described as negligible today. A new wholly owned subsidiary for sub-zero chillers (Aquilon) targets chemical, food and pharma, with commercial operations expected from next financial year.

segments.name: Data centre (oil-free / magnetic-bearing chillers)
segments.commentary: No data centre orders yet; the Danfoss Turbocor-based offering is sourced from an Australian partner. Management expects traction in 6-12 months and excludes data centre revenue from FY27 and FY28 projections.

guidance_outlook: Revenue to grow at about 40% CAGR; management reaffirmed this for FY27 and beyond, noting the guidance excludes data centre revenue.
EBITDA margin about 22% at annual level for FY27; H1 at 13.5% implies a steep H2 ramp, which management attributes to higher H2 volumes and product mix.
Working capital days expected to fall to about 350 days (CEO) and receivable days to about 200 days (CFO) over time.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by year-end FY27.
Order book expected to be healthy by year-end; management said orders will come in continuously rather than concentrated in Aug-Sep as last year.
Subsidy for the Karad unit 2 facility (Maharashtra D-class area) is not in projections and could add to margin.
capex_capacity: Unit 2 (Karad/Hanbarwadi) recently opened with about 50,000 sq ft in use; combined with unit 1 (about 20,000 sq ft) total manufacturing area about 70,000 sq ft.
Adjacent land of about 50,000 sq ft is already levelled, so a new shed can be built quickly if a new opportunity arises.
Management says current capacity is sufficient for guidance; no fresh equity needed unless a new opportunity emerges.
Unit 1 (about 20,000 sq ft) being converted into a full testing facility, including an ambient-controlled AC test room.
Small CapEx expected for the Aquilon sub-zero chiller initiative; a small manufacturing unit is being set up.
demand_pricing: Navy fleet support ship turnkey project is among about 10 live projects; management cites a large AC/HVAC/Ref plant order for the Indian Navy.

Management cites a market of about INR 2,750 crore over two years from naval ship approvals (about 1% share) and about INR 2,500 crore in non-naval shipbuilding (about 0.5% share), for an estimated INR 4,000-5,000 crore opportunity.
Next-generation corvette (NGC) orders reportedly cleared by CCS; management expects part of the orders to convert into firm orders in FY27 and the rest in FY28.
Eight orders are in the pipeline.
Imports reduced from about 30%+ to single digit in AC plants, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why are H1 margins low again, and what H2 margin is needed to hit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity (copper, metals) inflation on fixed-price contracts, offset by strategic sourcing and higher inventory. H2 is seasonally stronger due to higher volumes absorbing overheads and product mix. Management said the 22% guidance is annual, not half-yearly, and skewness should fade over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days high and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivable days fell from about 350 in FY25 to 250 at March 2026, were held at about 250 in H1 despite 84% growth, and should go to about 200. Management said there is no one-off and that shipyard milestone-based payments limit faster reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative and when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed negative operating cash flow of about INR 42 crore to strategic sourcing, H2 deliveries and higher receivables. Management expects cash flow to turn positive by the end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre plan and are orders expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no data centre orders yet; the oil-free/magnetic-bearing technology is sourced from an Australian partner, with no manufacturing in India until volumes justify it. Traction is expected in 6-12 months and is excluded from FY27-28 projections.

qa_highlights.question: Can capacity support 40% growth and are new capex or funds needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is sufficient for current guidance. Land is levelled for a further shed if needed. Funding would be raised only if a new opportunity needs it; the additional working capital is to come mainly from internal accruals and some bank borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the depreciation method changed to straight line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said straight-line depreciation better reflects asset use and was adopted in a year of heavy capex. No quantified impact was given on the call.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (copper, metals) on fixed-price contracts could compress margins if strategic sourcing is insufficient.
Negative operating cash flow and rising receivables (INR 128 crore) and inventory (INR 80 crore); working capital days were about 400 against a target of about 350.
Order book fell from INR 270 crore to about INR 200 crore; the H2 order ramp is not yet visible.
Dependence on naval shipbuilding timelines and government budget or election-related delays were raised as questions; management disputed the risk.
Data centre traction is unproven and excluded from guidance; management acknowledged no orders yet.
ROCE currently about 14-15% per analyst; management says the same capital base should lift returns as growth is funded by working capital.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the naval pipeline, with repeated reassurance on the 40% CAGR and 22% margin guidance. Cautious and somewhat evasive on H1 margin gap, cash flow and the data centre timeline, relying on H2 skew and sector explanations. Several answers were unclear or deflected, notably on the criminal case question.
key_quotes: We are growing at a 40% CAGR rate and we will continue to grow at 40% CAGR rate, definitely.
Our component of INR 2.75 lakh-crore is approximately 1%, which is INR 2,750 crore, is for the next two years.

We feel that we are still about 6 to 8 months, maybe even about a year away for that kind of traction and therefore, we do not actually include data centre business revenues either into this financial year nor into our projections for the next year.

adds.what: Unit 2 (Karad/Hanbarwadi) facility, about 50,000 sq ft, recently opened and in use (already operating, not a future addition)
Unit 1 (about 20,000 sq ft) being converted into a full testing facility with ambient-controlled AC test room
Aquilon sub-zero chiller small manufacturing unit (capex small, unquantified)

growth.why: Management reiterated about 40% revenue CAGR (excluding data centre) and about 22% FY27 EBITDA margin, with H1 revenue up about 84-85% YoY; delivery is backed by a 198.6-200 crore order book, Navy/corvette pipeline and ~50,000 sq ft unit 2 already in use, but the order book fell from 270 crore and H1 operating cash flow was negative 42 crore, so backing is only partial.

mgmt.note: Brief references a CEO giving working capital guidance, but no clear change in top management or new growth plan is stated in the brief.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 13.5% vs 11% last year and FY27 guided at about 22% annual, which needs a steep H2 ramp from higher volumes and mix, though commodity inflation on fixed-price contracts is a drag.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says current capacity (about 70,000 sq ft combined after Unit 2 opened) is sufficient for the 40% CAGR guidance, with no new shed planned unless a new opportunity emerges.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue about INR 100 crore, up 84-85% YoY, and management guides about 40% revenue CAGR, backed by a 198.6-200 crore order book and 8 pipeline orders, though the order book fell from INR 270 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, and management says no fresh equity is needed and only small capex is planned (Unit 1 testing conversion, Aquilon unit), so no major capex is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reiterated the 40% revenue CAGR and 22% EBITDA margin; with H1 margin at 13.5% and operating cash flow at negative INR 42 crore, there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must lift margin from 13.5% to about 22% annual, the order book fell from INR 270 to about INR 200 crore, and receivable days (about 250) and working capital (about 400 days vs 350 target) remain stretched.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aquilon sub-zero chiller subsidiary has commercial operations expected from next financial year (FY28), and data centre offering traction is expected in 6-12 months, but neither is in guidance and no orders exist yet.

rows.label: Naval fleet and NGC corvette orders converting to firm orders
rows.why: Management expects part of the cleared next-generation corvette orders to convert to firm orders in FY27 and the rest in FY28, with about 10 live projects and 8 pipeline orders, though the order book has fallen to about INR 200 crore.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turns positive and receivable days fall
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative INR 42 crore and receivable days were about 250; management targets positive cash flow by FY27 end and receivable days of 200 going forward, with shipyard milestone payments limiting pace.

rows.label: Karad unit 2 subsidy not in projections
rows.why: The Maharashtra D-class area subsidy for the Karad facility is excluded from projections and could add to margin, but no amount was quantified on the call.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 40% CAGR, naval pipeline and 22% margin guidance, but cautious and at times evasive on the H1 margin gap, negative cash flow and the data centre timeline, while analysts pressed on receivables, working capital and order book decline.
